hints: A substring has k ones when two prefix counts differ by k.
All positive differences can be counted together by convolution.
analogy: Count pairs of milestones whose labels differ by each possible amount.
example: For 101, the counts for k=0,1,2,3 are 1,4,1,0.
algorithm: Compute prefix sums of ones for all n+1 prefix positions and let f[v] count prefixes with sum v. For k=0, sum f[v]*(f[v]-1)/2. For positive k, the answer is sum over v of f[v]*f[v+k]. Obtain all these autocorrelation values by convolving f with its reverse using an NTT under two suitable primes and reconstructing exact integer coefficients by the Chinese remainder theorem. Print zeros beyond the total number of ones.
correctness: Prefix sums never decrease. For k>0, every pair of prefix positions whose values differ by k has the smaller value earlier and defines exactly one substring with k ones. For k=0, choosing any two distinct positions of the same prefix value defines one nonempty zero-one substring. Convolution computes exactly these pair counts.
complexity: For string length n, NTT convolution takes O(n log n) time and O(n) space; two moduli are needed to reconstruct counts up to n(n+1)/2 exactly.
